title: A combined Langendorff-injection technique for simultaneous isolation of single cardiomyocytes from atria and ventricles of the rat heart
author: Butova, Myachina, et al.

steps.title: Animal preparation and euthanasia
steps.instruction: Inject each adult Wistar rat (3–6 months old) intramuscularly with heparin sodium (5 000 IU · kg⁻¹). After 20 min anesthetize with Zoletil (0.3 mL · kg⁻¹) and Xylazine (1 mL · kg⁻¹). Euthanize the animal 15–20 min after anesthesia.

steps.title: Prepare heart and K‑H buffer
steps.instruction: Rapidly open the chest, flush the heart with cold (10–15 °C) heparin‑containing Krebs‑Henseleit (K‑H) buffer, then excise the heart with lungs and keep it in the same cold buffer without cutting the descending aorta, pulmonary trunk, venae cavae or pulmonary veins, and without removing the pericardium. Prepare K‑H buffer (pH 7.25, 35 °C) containing per litre: NaCl 58.44 g, KCl 74.55 g, MgSO₄·7H₂O 120.37 g, KH₂PO₄ 13.6 g, NaHCO₃ 84.01 g, HEPES 23.83 g, Taurine 125.15 g, Adenosine 267.24 g, d‑Glucose 180.20 g, CaCl₂ 110.98 g; equilibrate with 95 % O₂ + 5 % CO₂ for 30 min, calibrate pH, then add heparin sodium to a final concentration of 10 IU · mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Langendorff retrograde perfusion
steps.instruction: Transfer the heart to a pre‑warmed Langendorff apparatus (35.5 °C). Cannulate the aorta in <30 s, secure with an alligator clip and ligature thread. Perfuse at ~4.0–4.5 mL · min⁻¹ with heparinized K‑H buffer for 5 min after the heart resumes normal beating (80–110 bpm) to wash out blood. Then switch to low‑Ca²⁺, high‑K⁺ K‑H buffer (Table 2) for 10 min after the heart stops beating; ligate the pulmonary trunk and a vena cava, increase flow to 4.5–5.0 mL · min⁻¹, and monitor atrial enlargement and pallor as indicators of sufficient perfusion.

steps.title: Enzyme perfusion and atrial injection
steps.instruction: Perfuse the heart with low‑concentrated enzyme solution (Table 2) for 10–15 min at 5.2–5.5 mL · min⁻¹. After 2–2.5 min begin injecting each atrium with high‑concentrated enzyme solution (Table 3) at 0.5–1 mL · min⁻¹ using an insulin syringe, keeping all injections at the same puncture site. Continue retrograde perfusion until the heart reaches a half‑digested state (pale surface, soft, viscous drops at the apex). Immediately transfer the heart to a custom petri dish containing warm (35 °C) medium‑concentrated enzyme solution (Table 3) equilibrated with 95 % O₂ + 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Intraventricular injections
steps.instruction: Place the heart in a petri dish on a hot‑plate (35.5 °C). Fix the ascending aorta with an alligator clip; ligate the descending aorta and veins and secure them with hooks. Inject the left ventricular apex for 7 min at 5–6 mL · min⁻¹, then the right ventricular free‑wall apex for 12–15 min, and finally the interventricular septum (needle fully inserted) for 2–3 min, all at the same puncture site. Observe progressive atrial enlargement. Stop intraventricular perfusion when the epicardium becomes soft, glossy, shows holes and pale areas, emits the characteristic smell, and single myocytes appear in the bath. Keep 95 % O₂ + 5 % CO₂ supplied throughout.

steps.title: Separate chambers and intra‑atrial digestion
steps.instruction: Remove all ligatures and dissect the heart into five regions: left ventricular free wall, right ventricular free wall, interventricular septum, left atrium, right atrium. Transfer each region to a separate petri dish: (i) LV free wall and septum – low‑concentrated enzyme solution mixed 1:1 with stopping buffer; (ii) RV free wall – low‑concentrated enzyme solution alone; (iii) both atria – high‑concentrated enzyme solution alone. Gently mechanically disrupt the ventricular pieces, resuspend in stopping buffer, filter, and begin extracellular Ca²⁺ titration (see Step 6). For the atria, perform intra‑atrial injections of high‑concentrated enzyme solution for 20–24 min at 6–7 mL · min⁻¹ using separate syringes; keep the atria not completely hermetic, cut the atrioventricular septum, and maintain a flow of 6–7 mL · min⁻¹. Stop when atrial digestion signs (same as ventricles) appear.

steps.title: Generate single‑cell suspensions
steps.instruction: Finely mince all completely digested tissues with small scissors. For ventricular material, filter through a mesh, resuspend in stopping buffer, and allow gravity sedimentation for 10–12 min. For atrial material, centrifuge at 7 × g (200 rpm) for 2 min in stopping buffer, then gravity‑sediment. Repeat sedimentation cycles while gradually raising extracellular Ca²⁺ concentration according to Table 4: Step 0 (stopping buffer + medium‑conc enzyme 1:1) 0.025 mM Ca²⁺; Step 1 0.10 mM; Step 2 0.25 mM; Step 3 0.40 mM; Step 4 0.90 mM; Step 5 Hepes‑buffered Tyrode 1.8 mM. Store the final cell pellet in Hepes‑buffered Tyrode solution (Table 5) at 22–24 °C, keeping tubes at a 45° angle to prevent cell adhesion.
